notes.noEmailChannel: Email codes are accepted, but no email channel is set, so only the authenticator can be armed.
notes.sessionsFixed: The lifetime and its renewal are fixed in Polaris. The rest is set by each account for itself; there is no instance-wide switch.
notes.firstAdmin: The first administrator, made during setup, has no entry in the audit trail.
notes.chain: The chain shows an entry edited or removed after it was sealed. Removing the newest entries is caught only against a copy of the head kept outside Polaris.
notes.localUnencrypted: A copy kept on the disk of the thing it protects is written unencrypted by design; every copy that leaves it is encrypted.
notes.listShows: The list shows the {shown} most recently backed-up items of {total}; the figures above count them all.
notes.masterKey: Encrypted under the instance's master key, which is not stored in the database.
notes.builtInLimits: The limits Polaris puts on its own codes and link passwords are built in, not settings, and are not counted here.

chainBreak.missing: An entry is missing from the chain
chainBreak.altered: An entry was changed after it was sealed
chainBreak.relinked: An entry no longer points at the one before it

outside.disks: Whether the disks of the machines Polaris runs on are encrypted.
outside.copies: Where copies of the master key, the backup recovery keys and the audit chain head are kept outside this instance.
outside.older: Entries older than the audit log's retention period, and changes made before the trail recorded them.
outside.processes: The organization's own processes: access reviews, joiners and leavers, training, vendor management, incident response and physical security.

export.name: Name
export.noChange: No change to this area is recorded in the audit trail.
export.title: # Polaris configuration evidence
export.notCertified: Polaris is not certified against SOC 2 or ISO 27001. Certification is an audit of the organization that runs it; this report is evidence of how this instance was configured at the moment above.
export.attentionMeans: Items marked (attention) are protections that are off or checks that did not pass.
export.checking: The SHA-256 of an unchanged JSON export equals the value above. The same value is recorded, with who exported it and when, in the audit trail entry `evidence.export`.
